title: Flyweight

act2.summary: an allocation budget, measured - not a functional requirement

solutions.title: One StopMetadataFactory, shared by every StopTime
solutions.tradeoff: A StopMetadataFactory caches one StopMetadata per stop id, so 200,000 StopTimes allocate exactly three. The price: nothing but discipline stops a caller from building a StopMetadata object literal directly and quietly opting out of the sharing, and the guarantee is worthless without a test that actually counts allocations - a Map nobody measures is ceremony, not a trade.

reviewFocus: Does act2/tests/allocation-budget.test.ts actually assert a number, or does it just check that buildTimetable still runs?
Could any file other than StopMetadataFactory construct a StopMetadata object literal without the type system objecting?
Is ACT2.md honest that the baseline's fourteen extra lines are a Flyweight factory in every way but name?

Given STOP_DIRECTORY has three entries today, at what point would this drill's niche verdict flip - what has to be true about the shared data itself, not just the object count, for the factory to earn its keep?
